newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CSN says no definite job cut plans.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CSN says no definite job cut plans.

text.p: Brazilian steel company Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) has no definite plans to reduce its number of staff as part of its ongoing restructuring process, senior CSN executives said.

There has been widespread speculation that the steel firm which was privatized three years ago is planning to lay off some 2,000 workers, a move which was thought to be behind this month's resignation of CSN chief Sylvio Coutinho. The company has about 13,700 employees.
"CSN has no set program to cut jobs. The dismissal of large numbers of staff took place before privatization," said Maria Silvia Bastos Marques, director of CSN's corporate sector.
"CSN is restructuring within the general restructuring of Brazil. The survival of CSN depends on this (restructuring) program," she said.

She said CSN had to restructure to be a competitive player in the international market, but it was not possible to predict whether or how many people might be laid off as a result of the restructuring process.
Marques said CSN was looking to hire someone externally to replace Coutinho and take the place of the third of three directors who run the company jointly.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
